Sources

Putting booths on a map

Nobody publishes coordinates — these get surveyed on foot

Eight booths named for a World Showcase pavilion borrow that pavilion's published coordinate, good to roughly 30–50 m. 9 have no position at all — no source publishes one, and seasonal kiosks never make it into OpenStreetMap.

Open the studio → Open the survey tool → Drop a pin from a desk, or one tap per booth while you're standing there.

Data feed

What a client app downloads

The whole festival in one versioned file — 209 dishes across 32 booths, about 18 KB gzipped. Re-checking it costs nothing: unchanged data produces an identical file, so a returning client gets a 304 and no body.

v1/snapshot.json Integration notes →

Booths & menus

Dietary tags are inferred from menu wording, not from Disney's allergen data. A description names what a dish is sold on, not everything in it — "Carrot Cake" says nothing about the walnuts. Treat these as a way to browse, never as an allergen check, and ask at the booth.

Needs a human look

Fuzzy matches in the 70–89 confidence band, or menu items whose booth couldn't be confidently linked
